title: Singing without a microphone at the Grand Theatre in St. Louis
summary: At a St. Louis burlesque house he was the first singer in fifteen years who did not need a microphone.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Lee, also wasn't your voice so clear and loud on certain occasions, for example, like at the Grand Theatre in St. Louis, where they didn't need a microphone for you?

Oh, yes. I was appearing there back in 1948, I believe, or 49, somewhere along that area. I was appearing to Grand Theatre in St. Louis, the burlesque show at 6th and Market Street in St. Louis, Missouri. And Mr. Zeissler was the owner there. And I was appearing there as a song and dance act. And they had a microphone there, and naturally I was using the mic as usual. And they came back and took the microphone away from me. And they told me I was the first singer that had been in there in fifteen years that didn't have to have a microphone. They said I was deafening the people in the back with a microphone, and they could hear me just as plain without it as if they were sitting in the front row.
